title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
key_finding: Retrieval improves several knowledge-intensive tasks and makes provenance inspectable.
limitation_for_our_question: Does not track how one answer changes as a fixed ranking grows.
role_in_ear: Defines the RAG setting and terminology.

title: Retrieval Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
key_finding: Latent retrieval during pretraining improves knowledge-intensive downstream performance.
limitation_for_our_question: Trained retriever-reader coupling differs from black-box in-context augmentation.
role_in_ear: Contrasts learned retrieval with the present frozen-ranking setup.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
key_finding: Dense retrieval substantially improves top-k passage recall over a strong sparse baseline.
limitation_for_our_question: Retrieval recall does not reveal whether later passages reverse a correct generated answer.
role_in_ear: Motivates treating ranked retrieval prefixes as an experimental object.

title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering
key_finding: A generator can benefit from combining many retrieved passages.
limitation_for_our_question: Average top-k gains can conceal question-level damage and recovery.
role_in_ear: Provides the central counterpoint to reversal-focused analysis.

title: In-Context Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
setting_or_data: Frozen language models with prepended documents
key_finding: Unmodified LMs can use retrieved documents supplied directly in context.
limitation_for_our_question: Does not characterize adjacent correct-to-incorrect transitions.
role_in_ear: Closest foundation for the black-box prompting design.

title: HotpotQA: A Dataset for Diverse, Explainable Multi-hop Question Answering
key_finding: Supporting-fact labels allow evidence-sensitive multi-hop evaluation.
limitation_for_our_question: A 100-question distractor-dev slice cannot represent the full benchmark.
role_in_ear: Supplies questions and ranked candidate paragraphs.

title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
key_finding: Performance depends strongly on where relevant information appears in context.
limitation_for_our_question: Position effects are studied more directly than answer trajectories across nested prefixes.
role_in_ear: Motivates fixed order and explicit order controls in follow-up work.

title: Large Language Models Can Be Easily Distracted by Irrelevant Context
key_finding: Irrelevant information can sharply reduce reasoning accuracy.
limitation_for_our_question: Synthetic distraction does not reproduce a real retriever's nested ranking.
role_in_ear: Establishes that added context can cause genuine harm.

title: Making Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Robust to Irrelevant Context
setting_or_data: Open-domain QA with irrelevant retrieved passages
key_finding: Retrieval can reduce accuracy, while filtering and training improve robustness.
limitation_for_our_question: Does not center persistence, recovery, and retained beneficial repairs under fixed depth changes.
role_in_ear: Required filtering comparison and close conceptual overlap.

title: The Power of Noise: Redefining Retrieval for RAG Systems
setting_or_data: RAG with relevant and noisy passages
key_finding: Noise, ranking, and context composition interact in non-monotonic ways.
limitation_for_our_question: The intervention is broader than matched adjacent trajectory accounting.
role_in_ear: Motivates separating plausible distractors from generic noise.

title: How Easily Do Irrelevant Inputs Skew the Responses of Large Language Models?
setting_or_data: LLMs exposed to graded irrelevant inputs
key_finding: Even apparently irrelevant context can systematically steer model responses.
limitation_for_our_question: Does not use a frozen real retrieval ranking or measure recovery after reversal.
role_in_ear: Informs a mechanism-oriented distractor taxonomy.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
intervention_or_focus: Noise, rejection, integration, and counterfactual tests
key_finding: RAG systems vary substantially in noise robustness and information integration.
limitation_for_our_question: A broad benchmark does not isolate adjacent depth transitions.
role_in_ear: Provides diagnostic categories and external benchmark context.

title: Evaluating the Retrieval Robustness of Large Language Models
key_finding: Retrieval robustness varies with passage count and ordering.
limitation_for_our_question: Already covers retrieval-size degradation, so EAR cannot claim that idea as new.
role_in_ear: Closest depth-based overlap; EAR adds adjacent trajectories, persistence, recovery, and gate trade-offs.

title: Quantifying the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Against Spurious Features in Grounding Data
key_finding: Spurious grounding features cause sample-level transitions between correct and incorrect states.
limitation_for_our_question: Perturbed grounding differs from expanding one fixed real ranking.
role_in_ear: Closest metric overlap and an explicit novelty boundary.

title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
setting_or_data: RAG questions labeled for context sufficiency
key_finding: Knowing whether context is sufficient improves interpretation and selective answering.
limitation_for_our_question: Sufficiency alone does not optimize the joint harm-repair-coverage trade-off after an answer changes.
role_in_ear: Strong abstention and evidence-sufficiency baseline.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Conflicting Evidence
key_finding: Conflicting retrieved evidence exposes weaknesses in synthesis and answer selection.
limitation_for_our_question: Conflict is only one possible cause of an observed reversal.
role_in_ear: Supports conflict-aware follow-up analysis.

title: A Reality Check on Context Utilisation for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
setting_or_data: Real retrieved contexts annotated for reliability, sufficiency, difficulty, and stance
key_finding: Real retrieval quality has multiple dimensions that synthetic noise misses.
limitation_for_our_question: Does not follow the same question through nested retrieval depths.
role_in_ear: Motivates manual evidence audits and richer real-context labels.

title: Rational Synthesizers or Heuristic Followers? Analyzing LLMs in RAG-based Question-Answering
setting_or_data: 1,635 questions and 15,058 documents with grouped conflicting evidence
key_finding: Model conclusions often follow presentation heuristics rather than the strongest evidence.
limitation_for_our_question: Conflict groups are constructed rather than inherited from one retriever's ranking.
role_in_ear: Provides recent mechanism-level context for why answers can flip.

title: RAGAs: Automated Evaluation of Retrieval Augmented Generation
key_finding: Component-level automatic metrics help diagnose a RAG pipeline without gold references.
limitation_for_our_question: Evaluator scores are not substitutes for correctness transitions on labeled QA.
role_in_ear: Secondary evaluation option; gold-answer trajectory scoring remains primary.

title: ARES: An Automated Evaluation Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
intervention_or_focus: Context relevance, faithfulness, and answer relevance
key_finding: Synthetic training plus a small amount of human annotation can support automated RAG evaluation.
limitation_for_our_question: Judge quality and calibration introduce another model-dependent layer.
role_in_ear: Candidate evidence-support signal for a stronger gate.

title: RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
key_finding: Fine-grained human labels reveal hallucinations not captured by coarse correctness alone.
limitation_for_our_question: Hallucination annotation is not an adjacent retrieval-depth experiment.
role_in_ear: Separates correctness from faithfulness in interpretation.

title: Unanswerability Evaluation for Retrieval Augmented Generation
setting_or_data: Six categories of unanswerable RAG queries
key_finding: RAG systems need category-sensitive evaluation of whether to answer or reject.
limitation_for_our_question: Abstention on unanswerable inputs is not the same as reacting to evidence-induced answer changes.
role_in_ear: Required framework for coverage and abstention reporting.

title: Prompt-Based Abstention Fails Under Misleading Context: A Controlled Study of Small Frozen RAG Models
key_finding: Misleading evidence remains difficult: verification can reduce error while sacrificing correct-answer coverage.
limitation_for_our_question: Very recent preprint evidence has not yet received archival review.
role_in_ear: Reinforces reporting coverage and retained repairs alongside reversal reduction.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
intervention_or_focus: Learned reflection tokens and adaptive retrieval
key_finding: Joint retrieval and critique can improve factuality and controllability.
limitation_for_our_question: Requires training and a substantially heavier controller than a lexical diagnostic gate.
role_in_ear: Strong learned self-critique baseline for later work.

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation
setting_or_data: RAG tasks with compressed retrieved context
key_finding: Selective compression can remove unhelpful material and sometimes omit retrieval entirely.
limitation_for_our_question: Optimizes context before generation rather than responding to observed answer change.
role_in_ear: Filtering and compression baseline.

title: Corrective Retrieval Augmented Generation
key_finding: A retrieval-quality evaluator can trigger corrective search and document refinement.
limitation_for_our_question: More complex and not evaluated specifically on fixed-depth reversal retention.
role_in_ear: Retrieval-quality gate baseline.

title: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity
setting_or_data: Open-domain QA at different complexity levels
intervention_or_focus: Routing among no, single-step, and iterative retrieval
key_finding: Question complexity can guide how much retrieval and reasoning to use.
limitation_for_our_question: Routes before observing an answer change and does not measure beneficial repair retention.
role_in_ear: Query-level adaptive retrieval baseline.

title: Astute RAG: Overcoming Imperfect Retrieval Augmentation and Knowledge Conflicts for Large Language Models
setting_or_data: RAG with imperfect external evidence and internal knowledge
key_finding: Explicit consolidation improves robustness to imperfect or conflicting sources.
limitation_for_our_question: Requires richer reasoning and does not directly expose the minimal trajectory trade-off.
role_in_ear: Strong conflict-resolution baseline.

title: Stop-RAG: Value-Based Retrieval Control for Iterative Retrieval-Augmented Generation
key_finding: A controller can learn when further retrieval has insufficient value.
limitation_for_our_question: Training cost and iterative retrieval differ from deterministic frozen prefixes.
role_in_ear: Closest adaptive stopping comparison.

title: Instructing Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Explicit Denoising
key_finding: Explicit denoising instruction improves the use of noisy evidence.
limitation_for_our_question: Requires trained reasoning behavior and does not isolate adjacent reversal events.
role_in_ear: Denoising baseline and qualitative failure comparison.
